inputs.text: This is a real victory against oppressive state power. The Punjab and Haryana High Court granted regular bail to someone held under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, ruling that mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a person in Pakistan cannot justify prolonged incarceration. The individual was only allegedly in telephonic contact with a Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri.” Cases like this expose how these harsh laws act as tools of institutional control, letting the powerful lock people away on the flimsiest grounds and deepening structural inequalities that hit vulnerable groups hardest, especially those with cross-border ties rooted in our history of division and discrimination. Courts stepping up like this is essential for real reform and putting basic rights ahead of unchecked authority.
